The files in this folder hold data of the Autonomous Province of Trento,
measured by the automatic weather stations of its weather service,
Meteotrentino, and published on the province's open-data portal under
Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/:

    https://dati.trentino.it/dataset/dati-recenti-delle-stazioni-meteo
    https://dati.trentino.it/dataset/anagrafica-stazioni-meteo-stazioni-automatiche

    Dati: Provincia Autonoma di Trento - Meteotrentino, CC BY 4.0

The province says the values have not been validated and may hold errors.
They are not covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-22 from https://dati.meteotrentino.it/service.asmx,
without a key, with curl, one GET each. The answers hold no personal data
and no key. They are XML with CRLF line ends, encoded in UTF-8; every
file below keeps that.

    listaStazioni.xml   GET /listaStazioni          73,687 bytes, whole and
                        asked at 08:20:15 UTC       unchanged: 208 stations,
                                                    113 of them in service

    T0129.xml, T0193.xml, T0368.xml, T0406.xml, T0419.xml, T0420.xml
                        GET /ultimiDatiStazione?codice=CODE
                        asked between 08:21:47 and 08:22:59 UTC
                        CUT from answers of 89,355, 90,331, 85,651, 90,424,
                        58,484 and 75,223 bytes

A station's answer holds the station's values since midnight (UTC+1) at
the start of the day before, a row every quarter of an hour in each of
five sections. The cut keeps, in each section, the rows whose <data> is
2026-11-22T07:00:00 or later, every one of them byte for byte with its
indentation and line ends, and everything outside the rows as it was; a
section left without a row is written <name />, as the service writes an
empty section. So each file is the answer as it would be if the service
had kept its values from 06:00 UTC only. The six are the wind stations of
the southern box chosen for what they show: Paganella (T0406), Monte
Bondone (T0368), Torbole on Lake Garda (T0193) and Trento Laste (T0129),
with quarter hours that have a temperature and no wind; Tonadico (T0419),
whose answer has no humidity section; and Mezzano (T0420), whose
anemometer gave nothing after 03:45 (UTC+1), so that its cut answer has no
wind at all.

    listaStazioni_cut.xml is listaStazioni.xml cut down to nine stations:
    the head, the <anagrafica> entries of T0129, T0154, T0193, T0368,
    T0401, T0403, T0406, T0419 and T0420, each byte for byte and in the
    list's order, and the closing tag. T0154 is out of service since 2005,
    T0401 (Arco) has no anemometer, and T0403 (Ciampac) stands north of the
    southern box. A script checked that the whole list is its head, its
    entries and its closing tag, and that nothing else was changed.

    empty.xml           GET /ultimiDatiStazione?codice=T0436
                        asked at 08:22 UTC, 394 bytes, whole and unchanged:
                        the answer for Rifugio Alimonta, a station in
                        service that sent no values. The service answered
                        the same for a code it does not have, T9999.

On that day, at 08:22 UTC, the 113 stations in service answered with
5,855,161 bytes in all. 46 had wind in their answer: their answers were
3,810,764 bytes, 28 to 90 kB each. 7 answered with no values at all. The
46 are the adapter's list of wind stations.

The folder evening/ holds three answers of the service's other answer for
one station, asked at 08:25:43 to 08:25:47 UTC:

    evening/CODE.json   GET /datiRealtimeUnaStazione?stazione=CODE&h=90

for T0076 (Rabbi, San Bernardo), T0403 (Canazei, Ciampac) and T0404
(Marmolada, Sas del Mul): JSON, a row every five minutes from 15:30 (UTC+1)
on 2026-11-18, 470,082, 476,742 and 471,707 bytes. Each is CUT to the 13
rows from 2026-11-18T19:00:00+01 to 2026-11-18T20:00:00+01: the head, the
13 features byte for byte as the service wrote them, joined as in the
answer, and the closing "]}"; a script checked that every feature of the
whole answer is one the cut was taken from, and that the cut reads as
JSON. The adapter does not ask this answer: its licence is not stated
(see the manifest). These files are here for the next four.

listaStazioni_evening.xml is listaStazioni.xml cut down, as above, to the
entries of T0403, T0404 and T0076.

T0076_evening.xml, T0403_evening.xml and T0404_evening.xml are NOT
answers of the service as it gave them. They are a sample for the server's
development mode, whose clock stands at 19:05 UTC on 2026-11-18, four
days before this source was recorded, and the service's answer for a
station reaches back to the day before only. Each is written in the form
of the answer of 2026-11-22, with the head of empty.xml, <data> set to
2026/11/18, <tmin> and <tmax> nil and <rain> 0 as in empty.xml, empty
sections of rain and radiation, and in the sections of temperature, wind
and humidity a row for each quarter hour from 19:00 to 19:30 (UTC+1) at
which the row of evening/CODE.json of the same time has the value: wind
only at 19:00 and 19:30, the times at which the service's two answers were
seen to agree on the wind (on 2026-11-22, for Trento Laste, at all 63 full
and half hours; at a quarter past or to they did not). The sample ends at
19:30 and not at 19:45, of which evening/ has the temperature and the
humidity too: the wind of 19:45 is not known, and the development mode
shows a station's newest reading, which would then be one without a wind
for all three (the rows of 19:45 were in the sample until 2026-11-22, and
T0404_damaged.xml, made from it then, still has them). A value is written
as in evening/CODE.json, without a trailing ".0", as the service writes
its XML. So every value in the sample is one the service gave, for the
station and the moment the sample says. What the answer would have been
at 19:05 UTC is not known. A test of this crate holds the sample against
evening/.

listaStazioni_damaged.xml, T0404_damaged.xml and unavailable.html are not
the service's data: they are the evening sample with things changed by
hand, and a page written by hand, to test how the adapter reports what it
cannot read. The test that uses them says what was changed.

To record them again: fetch the list and the answers, cut them as above
(the counts the tests pin are of these stations and of that moment), set
the moment in tests/pipeline.rs, run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1
and review what changed. The evening sample stays as it is for as long as
the development mode's clock does.

A value in these files is what an instrument reported. It is no statement
that a place can be flown.
